title: Form effects driven by the paint event
blurb: Ink that arrives wet with each typed letter, a keypad that sinks round the pressed key, a colour input that lights its scene, a <progress> drawn as a tank of liquid and a search field that blurs the links that don't match. Each effect reads the control's state in the paint handler. Four of them have no listener on the control.
question: Can an effect on a form control be driven by the paint event alone, reading value, :active, :focus and position in the handler, with no input, pointer or focus listener?
result: Yes for four of the five, as long as the state changes a pixel of the control's picture. A touch press didn't set :active on a button drawn in a canvas (Chromium 157, emulated touch), so the pressed button has a pointerdown listener as a second route.
